attempted_claim: Fix a Diophantine class D(c,tau) with explicit constants c>0, tau>=0 and a regularity class of C^7 strictly convex closed planar curves with strictly positive curvature, fixed length L, curvature ratio bound K, and C^7 norm bound N. Define an explicit computable threshold Q*=Q*(L,K,N,c,tau) as a fixed closed-form function. Prove or disprove the following dichotomy: either every such curve possesses a smooth convex caustic for every Diophantine rotation number omega in D(c,tau) with 0<omega<=1/Q*, obtained as a KAM invariant circle in Lazutkin coordinates under a uniform smallness condition, or there exists one such curve satisfying the bounds L,K,N for which a stated Diophantine omega in D(c,tau) with omega<=1/Q* carries provably no convex caustic. A complete answer is a rigorous proof of the uniform Diophantine existence claim at the stated explicit threshold, or an explicit C^7 counterexample table with certified bounds plus a rigorous converse-KAM nonexistence proof at one such Diophantine rotation number.
